issue_title: RBF kernel PCA centering allocates multiple dense matrices and performs cubic products
pr_title: Center RBF kernel matrices with in-place mean subtraction
issue_body:
### Description

RBF kernel PCA centers its symmetric kernel as `K - J @ K - K @ J + J @ K @ J`, where `J` is a dense sample-square matrix of `1 / n_samples`. This allocates multiple additional dense matrices and performs cubic matrix products before eigendecomposition.

The same centering can be computed by subtracting the column and row means and adding the grand mean. Because the kernel is symmetric, one mean vector supplies both axes. These operations can update the kernel in place.

### Proposed change and evidence

Use in-place mean subtraction, retaining the existing kernel, eigendecomposition and projection behavior.

A real public `fit` and `transform` regression uses 4,000 samples with three features, after allowing 700 MiB of additional process address space. Unchanged master raises `_ArrayMemoryError` while allocating another 4,000-by-4,000 float64 matrix during centering (about 122 MiB for that allocation). The corrected implementation completes the full fit, including eigendecomposition, and produces finite results.

Twelve numerical controls compare fitted eigenvalues and reconstructed kernels with an independent dense `H @ K @ H` reference for ordinary, duplicated and constant datasets, two kernel coefficients and both copy settings.

On unchanged source `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`, the new module reports **1 failed, 12 passed**. With the fix, **85 feature-extraction/base tests pass**.

Only the centering stage changes from cubic matrix products to quadratic-time mean/subtraction operations. The full eigendecomposition still has cubic time and quadratic memory requirements; this is not an end-to-end timing benchmark.

[Successful validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/mlxtend/actions/runs/43670246125).
pr_body:
### Description

The RBF kernel centering formula builds a dense all-ones centering matrix and several dense products. The products are unnecessary: centering is equivalent to subtracting row/column means and adding the grand mean.

Use the symmetric kernel's mean vector and update the kernel in place. This removes sample-square centering matrices and cubic centering products while preserving fitted numerical results. Document that the full eigendecomposition retains its existing cubic-time/quadratic-memory cost.

### Validation

Base: `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`. Validated source: `66c12792d9c765dea68a7606a27c373fefaab77a`.

- Same 13 new regression/control cases on unchanged production source: **1 failed, 12 passed**.
- Feature-extraction and base-model tests after the fix: **85 passed**.
- A Linux subprocess runs real `RBFKernelPCA.fit` and `transform` on 4,000-by-3 data with 700 MiB of additional address space after imports. Original centering fails while allocating another 122 MiB matrix; the corrected implementation completes full eigendecomposition and returns finite results.
- Numerical controls compare fitted eigenvalues and reconstructed kernels against an independent dense `H @ K @ H` reference for ordinary, duplicated and constant datasets, two gamma values and both copy settings.
- Tests also verify zero centered-kernel row/column sums, projected-basis orthonormality, unchanged input and the existing copy/reference contract.
- Black, isort and Flake8 pass on both changed Python files, with a clean checkout check.
- Python 3.11.18, NumPy 2.4.0, SciPy 1.16.3, scikit-learn 1.8.0 with frozen uv dependencies on Ubuntu. The full repository suite and runtime/peak-RSS benchmarks were not run. The address-space regression is skipped on non-Linux platforms.

[Successful exact-commit validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/mlxtend/actions/runs/43670246125).

### Related work

Reviewed all-state kernel-PCA/centering history and the original #28 and later #151 diffs. All 34 pre-existing fork heads retain dense centering products, including the older kernel-PCA projection branch. That branch changes projection handling and stores means but still uses the original dense centering expression. This patch changes only the kernel-centering stage.

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added a changelog entry.
- [x] Added numerical controls and a full-public-fit allocation regression.
- [x] Documented centering and eigendecomposition costs.
- [x] Relevant tests and changed-file style checks pass.
